newsitem.title: USA: Hillary Clinton cites new parental guilt trip.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton cites new parental guilt trip.

text.p: Hillary Clinton said Friday that new research on early child development may send working parents, especially mothers, on a new guilt trip.

Clinton, in an interview from Princeton, New Jersey, on the ABC television programme "Good Morning America," referred to scientists' findings on the importance of parental stimulation during the first three years of life.
"I think that you're right that it does ratchet up the guilt," she told interviewer Charles Gibson before giving a keynote address to an early childhood development conference in Princeton.

"I mean guilt seems to be an occupational hazard of parenthood, particularly motherhood, no matter what the decisions we make might be," said Clinton, a long-time children's advocate and author of a best-selling book about child-rearing, "It Takes a Village."
"But I think that that guilt is misplaced unless we use it as a means of asking ourselves what is it we need to do to help parents do the best jobs they can," she added.

Recently published studies discussed at a White House conference on April 17 found that the number of words an infant hears each day from an attentive, engaged person is the single most important predictor of later intelligence, school success and social competence.
Clinton said she believed there was no "cookie-cutter answer" to suit all women as they wrestle with balancing any choices they must make between dividing their time between families and careers.
"I really believe that what we now know is that it's essential for parents to stimulate appropriately their children and that includes fathers as well as mothers," she said.
"Let's not let fathers off the hook here because they have a very important role to play in helping a child in those first three years of life.
"But I think the real answer to draw from this is that each woman has to look very hard at herself, at her situation, and make the decisions that are right for her," Clinton said.
